He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland Terrapins]] and was selected by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] with the 19th overall pick in the [[2018 NBA draft]]. ==High school career== Huerter, a {{cvt|6|ft|7|in}} [[shooting guard]], played at [[Shenendehowa High School]] in [[Clifton Park, New York]], a suburban town located in [[Saratoga County, New York|Saratoga County]]. During his career, he led the school to its second state championship and, as a senior, was named [[Mr. New York Basketball]].{{cite web|first=Don|last=Markus|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2016/04/08/maryland-basketball-signee-kevin-huerter-honored-by-high-school-turning-his-likeness-into-a-logo/|title=Maryland basketball signee Kevin Huerter honored by high school turning his likeness into a logo|work=[[Baltimore Sun]]|date=April 8, 2016|access-date=May 27, 2018}} He also played on the baseball team, and won the Class AA state championship in 2016 with future MLB pitcher [[Ian Anderson (baseball)|Ian Anderson]].{{Cite web |last=Milligan |first=Rashad |date=2018-09-19 |title=When Kevin Huerter and a top Atlanta Braves prospect won a baseball championship |url=https://www.peachtreehoops.com/2018/9/19/17877742/kevin-huerter-atlanta-hawks-ian-anderson-atlanta-braves-top-prospect-feature |access-date=2024-06-01 |website=Peachtree Hoops |language=en}} On September 7, 2015, Huerter committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], choosing the Terrapins over 20 offers.{{cite web|first=Brady|last=Farkas|url=http://1045theteam.com/kevin-huerter-signs-nli-with-maryland/|title=Kevin Huerter signs NLI with Maryland|work=1045theteam.com|date=November 12, 2015|access-date=May 27, 2018}} By the end of his high school career, Huerter was considered a four-star recruit and was ranked No. 50 overall recruit and No. 11 shooting guard in the 2016 high school class.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/211555/kevin-huerter|title=Kevin Huerter – Basketball Recruiting – Player [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] in 2017]] Huerter earned a starting position as a freshman, averaging 9.3 points and 4.9 rebounds per game on the season.{{cite web|first=Bill|last=Arsenault|url=https://www.timesunion.com/sports/article/Kevin-Huerter-makes-strides-with-Maryland-12736482.php#item-85307-tbla-4|title=Kevin Huerter makes strides with Maryland basketball|work=[[Times Union (Albany)|Times Union]]|date=March 7, 2018|access-date=May 27, 2018}} Following his freshman season, he was selected to the United States team for the [[2017 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]], where the team finished third.{{cite web|first=Scott|last=Greene|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/kevin-huerter-selected-final-usa-154438945.html|title=Kevin Huerter selected to final USA U19 roster|work=[[Yahoo Sports]]|date=June 22, 2017|access-date=May 27, 2018}} As a sophomore, Huerter increased his production, scoring 14.8 points and averaging 5 rebounds per game. At the close of the season, he was named honorable mention All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]].{{cite web|first=Tyler|last=Byrum|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/maryland-terps/cowan-fernando-huerter-receive-all-big-ten-honors|title=Cowan, Fernando, Huerter receive All-Big Ten honors|work=[[NBCSports.com]]|date=February 27, 2018|access-date=May 27, 2018}} ==Professional career== ===Atlanta Hawks (2018–2022)=== Following his sophomore season at Maryland, Huerter declared his eligibility for the [[2018 NBA draft]] without an agent.{{cite web |last=Markus |first=Don |date=April 20, 2018 |title=Maryland's Kevin Huerter will declare for NBA draft but will not sign with an agent |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2018/04/20/marylands-kevin-huerter-will-declare-for-nba-draft-but-will-not-sign-with-an-agent/ |access-date=May 27, 2018 |work=Baltimore Sun |archive-date=October 25, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181025133402/http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/tracking-the-terps/bs-sp-kevin-huerter-nba-draft-0420-story.html |url-status=live }} He was selected to participate in the [[NBA Draft Combine]].{{cite web |last=Byrum |first=Tyler |date=May 17, 2018 |title=Maryland's Kevin Huerter surprises at 2018 NBA Combine |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/maryland-terps/marylands-kevin-huerter-surprises-2018-nba-combine |access-date=May 27, 2018 |work=NBCSports.com}} After working out with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], Huerter opted to hire an agent and remain in the NBA draft, forgoing his final two years of college eligibility on May 30, 2018.{{cite web|first=Gary|last=Parrish|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/marylands-kevin-huerter-will-remain-in-the-nba-draft-dealing-a-big-blow-to-the-terrapins/|title=Maryland's Kevin Huerter will remain in the NBA Draft dealing a big blow to the Terrapins|work=[[CBSSports.com]]|date=May 30, 2018|access-date=May 30, 2018}} On June 21, 2018, Huerter was selected with the nineteenth overall pick by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]]. On July 1, 2018, Huerter officially signed with the Hawks.{{cite web |title=Hawks Sign Kevin Huerter, Omari Spellman And Trae Young |url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/hawks-sign-kevin-huerter-omari-spellman-and-trae-young# |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 2, 2018 |language=en}} On December 31, 2018, Huerter's first 20-point game came against the [[Indiana Pacers]], during which he scored 22 points in a 116–108 loss.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/id/401071218|title=Atlanta Hawks at Indiana Pacers Box Score, December 31, 2019|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=January 17, 2019}} On January 11, 2019, Huerter scored a season-high 29 points against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in a 123–121 victory.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/201901110PHI.html|title=Atlanta Hawks at Philadelphia 76ers Box Score, January 11, 2019|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=January 16, 2019}} At the end of the [[2018–19 NBA season]], Huerter was voted to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|All-Rookie Second Team]].{{cite web|url=https://www.peachtreehoops.com/2019/5/21/18618335/trae-young-nba-all-rookie-first-team-atlanta-hawks-kevin-huerter-voting-totals|title=Trae Young, Kevin Huerter garner All-Rookie honors|website=SB Nation|last=Rowland|first=Brad|date=May 21, 2019|access-date=June 28, 2021}} In game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semi-Finals against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], Huerter scored a playoff career-high 27 points, to lead the Hawks to their first [[2021 NBA playoffs|Eastern Conference Finals]] appearance since 2015.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2021/06/21/hawks-beat-76ers-game-7-kevin-huerter-trae-young-joel-embiid-nba-playoffs|title=Kevin Huerter Leads Hawks to Game 7 Win Over 76ers|website=Sports Illustrated|last=Selbe|first=Nick|date=June 19, 2021|access-date=June 28, 2021}} On October 18, 2021, Huerter signed a four-year, $65 million rookie contract extension with the Hawks.{{Cite web|title=Huerter, Hawks agree to contract extension|url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/atlanta-hawks/huerter-and-hawks-reach-agreement-for-extension/F2DUJDLWWBFQXPQPVMURBL6KTM/|access-date=October 18, 2021|website=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution}} ===Sacramento Kings (2022–2025)=== On July 6, 2022, Huerter was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in exchange for [[Maurice Harkless]], [[Justin Holiday]], and a future first-round pick.{{Cite web|title=Kings Acquire Kevin Huerter from Atlanta|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-acquire-kevin-huerter-from-atlanta|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2022|access-date=July 7, 2022}} On October 19, Huerter made his Kings debut, recording 23 points, three rebounds and two assists in a 115–108 loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{Cite web |title=GRANT RALLIES BLAZERS PAST KINGS 113-108 IN OPENER |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200014 |access-date=February 16, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On January 18, 2024, Huerter scored a career–high 31 points on 11–for–17 shooting in a 126–121 loss against the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{Cite web|title=Kings' Kevin Huerter: Nets career-high 31 points in loss|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kings-kevin-huerter-nets-career-high-31-points-in-loss/amp/|date=March 16, 2024|website=cbssports.com}} On March 21, Huerter was diagnosed with a dislocated left shoulder and labral tear after suffering the injury in a game against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web |agency=Associated Press | title=Kings guard Kevin Huerter is sidelined with injured left shoulder | website=NBA | date=2024-03-22 | url=https://www.nba.com/news/kings-guard-kevin-huerter-sidelined-left-shoulder-injury | access-date=2025-12-09}} On March 29, it was announced that he would undergo surgery to repair the injury, causing him to miss the remainder of the season as a result.{{Cite web|title=Sacramento Kings' Kevin Huerter to undergo season-ending shoulder surgery|url=https://www.nba.com/news/kevin-huerter-season-ending-surgery-left-shoulder-march-29|access-date=April 1, 2024|website=nba.com}} ===Chicago Bulls (2025–2026)=== On February 3, 2025, Huerter was traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in exchange for [[Zach LaVine]] and a 2028 second-round pick to the [[Sacramento Kings]], in a deal also involving the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|title=Bulls acquire Kevin Huerter, Zach Collins and Tre Jones in three-team deal|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-acquire-kevin-huerter-zach-collins-and-tre-jones-in-three-team-deal|website=NBA.com|date=February 3, 2025|access-date=February 3, 2025}} In 26 games (including 16 starts) for Chicago down the stretch, he posted averages of 13.2 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 3.2 assists. Huerter made 44 appearances (11 starts) for the Bulls during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging 10.9 points, 3.8 rebounds, and 2.6 assists.{{Cite web|title=Kevin Huerter 2025–26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4066372/kevin-huerter|access-date=February 9, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Detroit Pistons (2026–present)=== On February 3, 2026, Huerter was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] alongside [[Dario Saric]] for [[Jaden Ivey]] as part of a three team trade that also involved the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] swapping their 2026 first-round pick with Detroit and sending [[Mike Conley Jr.|Mike Conley]] to the Bulls.{{cite web|title=DETROIT PISTONS ACQUIRE KEVIN HUERTER AND DARIO SARIC FROM CHICAGO, DR.FT COMPENSATION FROM MINNESOTA |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-acquire-kevin-huerter-and-dario-saric-from-chicago-draft-compensation-from-minnesota|website=NBA.com|date=February 3, 2026|access-date=February 4, 2026}} He made 25 appearances (including three starts) for Detroit, averaging 8.6 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 2.5 assists. On June 29, 2026, Huerter re-signed with the Pistons on a three-year, $27 million contract.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=June 29, 2026 |title=Sources: Pistons' Kevin Huerter to return on 3-year, $27M deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49219769/sources-pistons-kevin-huerter-return-3-year-27m-deal |access-date=June 30, 2026 |website=espn.com |language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA
